title: Recipe 16 — Slash Commands (expansion at the user layer, before the model)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “A slash command is a markdown template the user triggers. The expansion happens at the user layer — the model never sees the slash.”

beats.label: Blank the scratch spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed recipe is never touched by a take.

beats.label: Blank the scratch settings
beats.cue: “The pre-slash hook lives in <cwd>/.crewhaus/settings.json — we'll come back to this file at the end.”

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env for the run beat — typing /review for real means calling the model.

groups.title: Beat 1 · the harness commands attach to

beats.label: Type recipe 01's harness
beats.cue: “Slash commands are data, not spec surface — so start from the plainest recipe-01 agent and change nothing.”

beats.label: Lint it
beats.cue: “Clean before a single command exists — so anything that changes downstream is the commands' doing.”

beats.label: Type the recipe's /review command
beats.cue: “One markdown file per command. Optional frontmatter for the /help line, then a body where $ARGUMENTS is the only moving part.”

beats.label: Add /release
beats.cue: “Same shape, and $ARGUMENTS appears twice — patch, minor or major flows into both the version bump and the prose.”

beats.label: Add /explain
beats.cue: “Third one — and the one we'll use to prove the substitution is literal, not parsed.”

beats.label: List the project layer
beats.cue: “Commands are file-discovered, so listing the directory is how you see what the runtime found.” Project layer wins over user and plugin.

verify.note: explain.md, release.md, review.md — the project layer at <cwd>/.crewhaus/commands

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “No trace of a slash command in the IR. They're runtime data read from the working directory — which is why no spec change was needed.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target cli — no slashCommands field in it

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it from this directory — so the boot that runs is the one that loads our three commands. GREEN, no key.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (11 anchors); install ok; boot gated at the provider credentials gate

beats.label: Find the command wiring in the emitted agent
beats.cue: “One field: slashCommands, handed to runChatLoop. wireMemory found them from cwd. Nothing generated, nothing hidden.”

beats.label: Run the real expander, keylessly
beats.cue: “loadCommands plus expand — the actual runtime functions, from the bundle we just checked. No model involved: this is a string operation.”
beats.command: bun --cwd live/dist -e 'import { loadCommands, expand } from "@crewhaus/slash-commands"; const c = await loadCommands({ cwd: "../..", homeDir: "/nonexistent" }); console.log("commands: " + [...c.keys()].sort().join(", ")); const r = expand("/review 1234", c); console.log("handled=" + r.handled + "  arguments=" + r.arguments + "\n--- expansion ---\n" + r.expanded)' > live/expansion.txt

verify.note: keyless. homeDir is pinned off the operator's real ~/.crewhaus/commands so the take is deterministic; redirect, not a pipe, so the exit code is bun's

beats.label: Read what the model would receive
beats.cue: “Eleven lines, and every $ARGUMENTS is now 1234. This — not `/review 1234` — is the user message the model gets.”

beats.label: Prove the substitution is literal
beats.cue: “Dollar-one stays dollar-one, dot-star-foo stays dot-star-foo, and an unknown name is handled=false — passed through untouched rather than guessed at.”
beats.command: bun --cwd live/dist -e 'import { loadCommands, expand } from "@crewhaus/slash-commands"; const c = await loadCommands({ cwd: "../..", homeDir: "/nonexistent" }); for (const raw of ["/explain $1", "/explain .*foo", "/nope 1"]) { const r = expand(raw, c); console.log(JSON.stringify(raw) + " -> handled=" + r.handled + " arguments=" + JSON.stringify(r.arguments)); }'

verify.note: measured: "$1" and ".*foo" survive verbatim (replaceAll on the literal placeholder), and /nope resolves to nothing so handled=false

beats.label: Type the recipe's pre-slash hook
beats.cue: “A hook that can rewrite or refuse an expansion before it reaches the model — allow, deny, or allow-with-mutate.”

beats.label: Prove it is valid JSON
beats.cue: “A malformed settings.json is the most common hooks bug — check it before the runtime does.”

verify.note: settings.json parses; the hook body itself is shell, executed only when a slash command fires

groups.title: One more thing · type it for real

beats.label: Launch the REPL
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Same spec as recipe 01. The difference is three markdown files and a hook it found on the way up.”

verify.note: CREWHAUS_TRACE=pretty is the recipe's own way to watch expansions at the user-message level; the chat loop needs Anthropic credentials

beats.label: Type the slash command
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Watch the trace: [slash:review] expanded args=1234, then the expanded user message. The model only ever sees the second one.”

verify.note: pre-slash hook returns allow (the recipe's hook only mutates /deploy), then the expansion is sent as the user turn

beats.label: Exit the REPL
beats.cue: [needs-key] “exit” returns to the shell.
